prompt: Changing a response field's type would break mobile app versions still installed on users' phones.
tells: break mobile app versions still installed
why: Release the change as v2; keep v1 until old apps are gone.

prompt: Adding a new optional field to a response doesn't require a new version, but removing one does.
why: Additive changes are compatible; breaking ones need a version.

prompt: Clients of v1 receive a Deprecation header and a sunset date months ahead.
why: Planned deprecation is part of versioning.
trap: Headers here communicate lifecycle, not auth.

prompt: Each API customer is pinned to the version from the date they signed up, and upgrades when they choose.
tells: pinned to the version from the date they signed up

prompt: Clients choose the API version with an Accept header instead of the URL path.
tells: Accept header instead of the URL path
why: Header-based versioning is one style; path-based is another.
trap: Same pattern, different place for the version.

prompt: Adding a new value to a status enum crashed older mobile apps that only expected three values.
tells: new value to a status enum
why: Some "additive" changes break strict clients; version them or document tolerant parsing.

prompt: Before shutting down v1, you check logs to see which customers still call it.
why: Measure usage before retiring a version.

prompt: In a GraphQL API, a field is marked @deprecated with a reason while a replacement is added.
why: GraphQL evolves by deprecating fields instead of versioning URLs.
